## What was wrong
The ported code returned the last Newton iterate `z`, which can sit one unit above the true root (e.g. raw `9999999998` → `9999999999`). The fix, matching Vyper PR 4486, takes the minimum of the last two iterates instead.

## Change (`candidate/Solution.lean` only)
- Defined `sqrt := vyperSqrtWith minFin` with `minFin y z = if y < z then y else z`, so the deployed-loop requirement holds by definition.
- Proved all 5 required theorems with their exact names and statements, no `sorry`.

## Proof sketch
Since core Lean has almost no Nat-sqrt theory and no `ring`/`nlinarith`, the proof builds everything from scratch: floor existence by induction, Newton-step bounds for `f(z) = (S/z + z)/2` (stays above the floor; error at least halves while above `r+1`; `f(r) ∈ {r,r+1}`, `f(r+1) = r`), seed above floor via a completing-the-square argument in `Int`, iterates confined to range (so no revert), convergence within 167 steps with stability after, then a fuel-indexed induction linking the spec `loop` to the Nat sequence. The two seed-fixed inputs (`9999999999`, `10000000000`) are discharged by direct computation.

## Verification actually run
- `lake build Solution` passes with no errors.
- Locked files all byte-identical (`locked.json` hashes match); only `candidate/Solution.lean` changed.
- No forbidden tokens in the file; imports unchanged.
- Axioms: `sqrt`, `neg_reverts`, `deployed_loop` use none; the other three use only `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, all permitted. Theorem types match the challenge exactly.
- Runtime differential test against Python `math.isqrt`: all outputs match, including `9999999998 → 9999999998`, edge cases (`0`, negatives → revert, `MAX_DECIMAL`), plus a 233-case randomized batch where every result satisfied `r² ≤ x·10¹⁰ < (r+1)²`.
